title: The Heron King
text: A heron taller than a man stands in the shallows on one leg, grey as the fog, wearing a crown of woven reeds. His eye is yellow and cold. He asks, with great courtesy, for a fish. Herons, the marsh folk say, remember every slight.

options.label: The quickest hands catch him a fish.

outcomes.text: He swallows it whole, and bows, and shows you a dry path through the marsh.
He stalks off into the fog. The marsh is less friendly after, and it remembers.
Just reeds, and a curse, and he will remember this slight forever.
